To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of a single gene tree to infer the species tree is a valid approach when there are many gene trees and the gene tree topology is highly accurate, 2) the use of gene tree topologies is a valid approach to infer the species phylogeny even if there is no accurate gene tree, and 3) gene trees can be inferred from gene order data with high accuracy, and the accuracy can be further increased by combining multiple data sources.
the gene tree is not a sufficient statistic of the species tree and that the distribution of gene trees under the coalescent is highly dependent on the gene tree.

the gene order of a bacterial genome can be used as a phylogenetic signal and that the accuracy and reliability of gene order-based phylogenetic reconstruction can be improved by using multiple gene orders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How to construct phylogenetic trees based on the order of genes in the genomes of species?
the development and evaluation of phylogenetic inference methods for genome-wide data, with a particular focus on gene order data and the use of multiple data types.
the problem of inferring phylogenetic trees from gene order data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the phylogenetic reconstruction based on gene order is a powerful and promising method to infer the evolutionary relationship of genomes, especially for closely related genomes with high similarity in sequence and structure.
the use of gene order data in phylogenetics has been shown to provide accurate results, even for large data sets, but the accuracy is dependent on the quality of the data.
there is no clear answer to the question of whether gene order is more informative than sequence for phylogenetic analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to accurately reconstruct the phylogeny of a large set of bacterial genomes, using only their gene-order information.
we have developed a method for reconstructing phylogenetic trees from gene-order data that is accurate, scalable and fast.
we have developed a method for accurate and fast phylogeny reconstruction from gene-order information that is applicable to a wide range of species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we now have a much more accurate and efficient way to infer phylogenetic trees from gene-order data than the previous methods.
gene-order data can be very informative for reconstructing phylogenetic trees and, when combined with gene content data, it can be used to reconstruct trees with high accuracy.
we can accurately and efficiently reconstruct phylogenies from gene orders.
